clue.text: For simple meal cover pan with a lid, almost

parts.note: a jacket is an outer covering
a pot is a cooking pan

indicators.note: almost means the word for lid loses its final letter

parts.note: a top is a lid

explanation.surface: Advice for a quick supper: put a pan on, nearly covered by its lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TOP to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked potato in its skin is a classic plain, filling dish for a light supper.

clue.text: Spear small pig-like animal finally shot

indicators.note: finally shot means the animal's last letter is removed, shot away

parts.note: a javelina is a peccary, a small pig-like American mammal

explanation.surface: A hunter brings down a small wild pig with a spear at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally shot' removes the last A of JAVELINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A javelin is a light throwing spear.

clue.text: Measure of cold, in short

parts.note: the letter C stands for cold on a tap, and is also the short form of a temperature scale

explanation.walkthrough: The scale named after Anders Celsius is abbreviated to C, the same letter that marks the cold tap.
explanation.definitionFit: This temperature scale measures how cold things are, and its abbreviation is C.

clue.text: Harry, he tears up flower

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone harasses a man who weeps while picking a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword pun: a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, and this is the great river of Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Place support for some Highland dress

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in addresses
aid means support or help

explanation.surface: A spot is found to give help to someone in Scottish costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is the tartan cloth worn over the shoulder as part of traditional Scottish dress.

clue.text: Bad weather intervenes in start of course for student

indicators.note: intervenes in means one piece comes between the letters of the other

parts.note: on a golf course play starts from the tee
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: Rain interrupts the opening of a course for a learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of course' looks like a first-letter pick; it is the golf tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone being taught a job, so a learner or student.

clue.text: Destroy American railway signal

definitions.meaning: to wreck a plan or ship completely, as with a self-propelled underwater missile
in the US a small explosive charge placed on the rails to warn train drivers

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to sink a ship or wreck a plan, and in the US a detonator used on railway tracks.

clue.text: Cheddar mine's incredibly sold

indicators.note: incredibly suggests something unbelievable has happened, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word mine's supplies its letters with the s

explanation.surface: My Cheddar cheese has sold amazingly well.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchandised means promoted and sold as goods.

clue.text: Cut loose even before that cover up

indicators.note: before means the shuffled letters come ahead of the word for cut
loose means the letters are set free and rearranged

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim loose material evenly before covering it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' reads as the verb of an instruction; it is the synonym, and 'loose' scrambles even, with 'before' placing that ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up or enclose completely.

clue.text: Mix up a badger with sheep

parts.note: to badger is to nag
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Confusing a badger with a sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badger' is a verb here, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram is a jumble of letters, so a mix-up.

clue.text: Start of week and star turn in means of sabotage

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday, the start of the week
key means principal, as a star player is
a wrench is a violent twist or turn

explanation.surface: A star act at the start of the week turns into a way of wrecking things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of week' is not a first-letter pick but the abbreviation MON.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a spanner of this kind into the works is the idiom for sabotage.

clue.text: Ship's officer left with whopper, right

definitions.note: the definition reads ship is, the 's being a link

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
a whopper is a big lie

explanation.surface: A ship's officer leaves after telling a huge lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship's officer' looks like one phrase; 'Ship' is the definition and 'officer' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a ship built to carry coal.

clue.text: Imprison old debt collector gone astray

parts.note: a dun was a person employed to demand payment of debts, an old use

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former bailiff has gone missing and must be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' turns GONE into GEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To lock someone in an underground cell, a verb use of the name for a castle prison.

clue.text: Little trips Jack leaves for relatives

indicators.note: leaves means the jack departs from the word for trips

parts.note: jaunts are short pleasure trips
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: Jack skips short outings with his family.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing J from JAUNTS leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives, sisters of a parent.

clue.text: Eg Major with duty is eponymous character

parts.note: Major is an example of a title, a military rank
a role is a function or duty

explanation.surface: A Major on duty plays the lead in a story named after him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' tempts as John Major, the former Prime Minister; here it is a rank used as a title.
explanation.definitionFit: The part whose name a play or film bears is its eponymous character.

clue.text: Sofa designed for intimate conversation

definitions.meaning: an S-shaped settee seating two people facing each other
a private talk between two people, French for head to head

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for head to head names both a private chat and a two-seat sofa made for one.

clue.text: Crockery resident abused around noon

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the letter for noon
abused means mistreated, so the letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone living there has mistreated the dishes at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges RESIDENT into DINERSET, and 'around' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching set of plates and dishes for serving the main meal is crockery.

clue.text: Married we turn up during midday at start of month

indicators.note: during means the reversed letters go inside the word for midday

parts.note: noon is midday

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: A couple who wed arrive at noon at the beginning of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses the married abbreviation plus we, giving EWM; in a down clue that reads upwards. 'during' places it inside midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar month begins with the moon unseen, the phase astronomers call the start of the cycle.

clue.text: I choose European person to read lesson

definitions.note: the definition speaks as a voter, one who chooses

parts.note: a lector reads the lessons in a church service

explanation.surface: A European speaks of choosing someone to read in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the answer itself is speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter is a person who chooses, so the answer can say it of itself.

clue.text: Where the funny bone is the French twist and bend

indicators.note: twist means the French article is turned round

parts.note: le is French for the
to bow is to bend

explanation.surface: French dancers twist and bend, knocking the funny bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' turns LE into EL.
explanation.definitionFit: The funny bone is the ulnar nerve at the joint in the middle of the arm.

clue.text: Copy long-legged bird coming after time

parts.note: the emu is a long-legged flightless Australian bird
arriving after the due time is being late

explanation.surface: A long-legged bird arrives after the appointed time and copies others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' tempts as T; the whole phrase 'coming after time' means LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to imitate or copy someone you admire.

clue.text: Scathingly attack second-rate celeb?

definitions.meaning: to criticise fiercely, as in a searing review
a ..., a celebrity of the second rank, the question mark flagging the wordplay

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to criticise harshly, and split up it gives a celebrity from the B list.

clue.text: Lumberjacks noticed beginning to reply in affirmative

parts.note: saw means noticed

indicators.note: in means that first letter goes inside the affirmative word

parts.note: yes is an affirmative reply

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of reply is taken

explanation.surface: Woodcutters noticed someone starting to say yes.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the first letter of 'reply', sits inside YES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawyers are people who saw timber, a lumberjack's trade.

clue.text: That is to say criticism is rubbish

parts.note: sc, short for Latin scilicet, means that is to say
a rap is a rebuke or criticism

explanation.surface: Namely, the critic says the work is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is a Latin abbreviation used in footnotes, like viz.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap is waste material, junk or rubbish.

clue.text: I have come after a coach, that's insulting

indicators.note: come after means the contracted I have follows the other pieces

parts.note: a coach is a bus
I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: I have arrived after the coach and someone is being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' tempts as a trainer; here it is a road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive means insulting and offensive in speech.

clue.text: Pick in ground, dire measure in US

indicators.note: in means the word for pick goes inside the rearranged letters
ground means crushed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to opt is to pick or choose

explanation.surface: A pick in the dire ground of America measures something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges the four letters to DIER, and 'in' puts the word for pick inside them. The British spelling ends -TRE, hence 'in US'.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of lens power is spelt this way in American English.

clue.text: What holds up laciest pants!

indicators.note: pants as a verb, gasps, but read as rubbish or awry, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what keeps up the laciest underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like underwear; it signals the rearrangement of LACIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic in a waistband is what keeps the garment from falling down.

clue.text: Pair in course run back around European businessman

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for pair goes inside the word for course

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

indicators.note: around means the reversed word surrounds the letter for European
back means the word run is read in reverse

parts.note: the word run is used as written

explanation.surface: A pair on a course run back past a European businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RUN into NUR, which 'around' puts round E.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepreneur is someone who sets up and runs businesses.
